title: Chili-Lemon Roasted Whole Trout with Garlicky Greens
dek: Two whole trout roast with lemon, garlic, parsley, and gentle chile heat while a quick pan of garlicky greens turns them into a complete dinner.
image_alt: Two roasted whole trout with lemon wedges, chopped chile, garlic, parsley, and fresh greens in a metal roasting pan
ingredients: 2 whole rainbow trout, cleaned and scaled, 1 to 1 1/4 lb each
3/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
5 garlic cloves, 3 finely grated and 2 thinly sliced
1/2 cup packed flat-leaf parsley leaves, plus tender stems for the fish cavities
12 oz baby spinach or tender mixed greens

instructions.name: Heat the oven and dry the trout
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center. Line a rimmed half-sheet pan with parchment. Pat the trout dry inside and out, including around the fins; dry skin roasts instead of steaming. Cut three shallow diagonal slashes through the skin on each side of each fish.

instructions.name: Build the chili-lemon seasoning
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons olive oil, the grated garlic, fennel seeds, red pepper flakes, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Finely grate 1 teaspoon zest from one lemon into the bowl, then cut that lemon into thin half-moons. Cut the second lemon into serving wedges.

instructions.name: Season and fill the fish
instructions.text: Rub the seasoned oil over both sides of the trout and into the slashes. Season the cavities with 1/4 teaspoon salt, then fill each with half the lemon half-moons and a few parsley stems. Arrange the fish at least 2 inches apart on the prepared pan.

instructions.name: Roast to safe doneness
instructions.text: Roast for 18 to 23 minutes, depending on thickness, until the flesh is opaque and flakes cleanly at the thickest point. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest flesh without touching bone should register 145°F. Rest the trout on the pan for 3 minutes.

instructions.name: Wilt the garlicky greens
instructions.text: While the fish roasts, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the greens, water, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Toss for 2 to 4 minutes until just wilted and glossy.

instructions.name: Finish and portion
instructions.text: Transfer the trout to a platter with the greens. Scatter with parsley leaves and serve with the lemon wedges. To portion, lift the top fillet away from the backbone, remove the backbone in one piece, and divide the lower fillet; check each serving for pin bones.

why_it_works: Slashing and thoroughly drying the skin lets heat reach the thickest flesh while limiting surface steam.
Lemon in the cavity perfumes the fish without flooding the skin with juice and making it soggy.
The greens cook during the trout's final minutes, so the complete dinner reaches the table hot without crowding the roasting pan.
swaps: Use two cleaned branzino of similar weight; begin checking at 17 minutes and rely on the thermometer.
Replace spinach with chopped Swiss chard; sauté the sliced stems for 3 minutes before adding the leaves.
For a dairy-free dinner, replace the butter with another tablespoon of olive oil.
storage: Remove the flesh from the bones before refrigerating. Store fish and greens in separate airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat covered in a 300°F oven with a teaspoon of water until the center reaches 165°F; the greens can be rewarmed briefly in a skillet. Do not freeze the cooked greens, which become watery.
notes: Ask the fish counter to clean and scale the trout, but inspect the cavities and rinse away any remaining bloodline only if needed; pat completely dry afterward.
USDA guidance for fish is 145°F at the thickest part. The flesh should also be opaque and separate easily with a fork.
Whole fish contains small pin bones. Portion carefully and remind diners to check each bite, especially when serving children.

faqs.q: How do I know whether a whole trout is scaled?
faqs.a: Run the back of a knife gently from tail toward head. A properly scaled fish feels smooth; if rough scales lift, scrape them off over the sink and rinse briefly before drying very well.

faqs.q: Can I roast trout fillets instead?
faqs.a: Yes. Use four 5- to 6-ounce skin-on fillets, omit the cavity aromatics, and begin checking after 8 minutes at 425°F. Cook to 145°F at the thickest point.

faqs.q: Is the chile level very spicy?
faqs.a: No; 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes gives gentle warmth across four servings. Reduce to 1/4 teaspoon for sensitive eaters or pass extra flakes at the table.

title: Miso-Glazed Eggplant with Herby White Bean Tahini & Seed Crunch
dek: Jammy miso-maple eggplant rests on a lemony white bean and tahini cream, finished with scallion curls, herbs, and a crackly toasted seed topping.
image_alt: Charred miso-glazed eggplant half on pale green herb tahini with curled scallions, cilantro, herb oil, and toasted seed crunch
ingredients: 2 large globe eggplants, about 1 lb each
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or gluten-free tamari
1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
3/4 cup packed cilantro leaves and tender stems, divided
1/3 cup ice water, plus more as needed

instructions.name: Score and salt the eggplant
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Halve the eggplants lengthwise and score the flesh in a 1-inch crosshatch without cutting through the skin. Sprinkle the cut sides with 3/4 teaspoon salt and leave them cut-side up for 10 minutes, then blot away the surface moisture.

instructions.name: Start the roast
instructions.text: Brush a rimmed sheet pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Rub 2 tablespoons oil over the eggplant flesh, working it into the cuts. Arrange cut-side down and roast for 25 minutes, until the undersides are deeply browned and the centers are beginning to soften.

instructions.name: Whisk the miso glaze
instructions.text: Whisk the miso, maple syrup, soy sauce, 1 teaspoon rice vinegar, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Turn the eggplant cut-side up, brush the glaze across the flesh, and return it to the oven for 10 to 15 minutes, until glossy, dark at the edges, and completely tender when pierced.

instructions.name: Blend the herby white bean tahini
instructions.text: Meanwhile, blend the cannellini beans, tahini, garlic, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, half the cilantro, 1/2 teaspoon salt, the remaining 1 teaspoon rice vinegar, and the ice water until very smooth. Add 1 tablespoon more water if needed for a thick swooping consistency. Taste and adjust with lemon.

instructions.name: Toast the seed crunch
instructions.text: Put the sunflower seeds, sesame seeds, coriander, red pepper flakes, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt in a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and the sesame seeds are golden. Transfer immediately to a plate.

instructions.name: Curl the scallions and assemble
instructions.text: Thinly slice the scallions lengthwise and soak them in ice water for 5 minutes to curl, then drain and dry. Spread the bean tahini across a platter, set the glazed eggplant on top, and finish with the seed crunch, scallion curls, remaining cilantro, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and lemon wedges.

why_it_works: Roasting cut-side down first concentrates the eggplant's moisture and creates a browned surface before the sugary glaze is introduced.
White beans give the tahini base enough body and protein to turn a vegetable centerpiece into a satisfying main course.
Toasted seeds, fresh herbs, and crisp scallions counter the eggplant's soft texture with crunch and brightness.
swaps: Use four smaller Italian eggplants and begin checking them 5 minutes earlier.
Replace sunflower seeds with chopped roasted pistachios or pumpkin seeds.
Use parsley in place of cilantro, or combine the two for a milder herb flavor.
storage: Refrigerate the roasted eggplant, bean tahini, and seed crunch separately for up to 4 days. Reheat the eggplant cut-side up in a 350°F oven for 10 to 12 minutes; serve the bean tahini cool or at room temperature and add the seed crunch only after reheating. Freeze the bean tahini for up to 1 month, but do not freeze the assembled dish.
notes: The eggplant is done when a knife slides through the thickest part with almost no resistance; undercooked eggplant will taste spongy.
White miso is gentler and slightly sweeter than red miso. If using red miso, reduce it to 1 1/2 tablespoons and taste before adding extra salt.
For a strictly gluten-free plate, use tamari labeled gluten-free and verify the miso packaging.

faqs.q: Do I need to peel the eggplant?
faqs.a: No. The skin holds each half together while the center becomes spoon-tender. Diners can eat the skin or scoop the glazed flesh away from it.

faqs.q: Can I make the white bean tahini without a blender?
faqs.a: Yes. Mash the beans very thoroughly, whisk in the tahini and seasonings, then press the mixture through a fine sieve for a smoother result. It will be more rustic but still flavorful.

faqs.q: Why add the miso glaze late?
faqs.a: Miso and maple brown quickly. Adding them after the eggplant is mostly tender lets the glaze caramelize without scorching during the full roast.

title: Rustic Cardamom Plum Galette with Almond Crust
dek: A free-form late-summer tart with jammy red plums, warm cardamom, and a tender almond-yogurt crust that needs only a brief freezer rest.
image_alt: Rustic plum galette in a dark metal pan with a flaky folded crust, glossy red plum filling, a plated slice, and fresh halved plums
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (180 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
8 tbsp (113 g) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1/3 cup (80 g) cold plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
1 tbsp ice water, only if needed
1 1/2 lb ripe but firm red plums, pitted and cut into 1/4-inch wedges

instructions.name: Make the quick almond pastry
instructions.text: Whisk the all-purpose flour, almond flour, 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a wide bowl. Cut in the cold butter with a pastry blender or fingertips until most pieces are pea-size. Fold in the yogurt. Squeeze a handful; if it will not hold, add the ice water 1 teaspoon at a time.

instructions.name: Roll and briefly chill
instructions.text: Turn the shaggy dough onto a lightly floured sheet of parchment and press it together without kneading. Roll into a roughly 13-inch circle about 1/8 inch thick. Slide the parchment and dough onto a rimmed sheet pan and freeze for 15 minutes while you heat the oven to 400°F and prepare the plums.

instructions.name: Season the plum filling
instructions.text: In a large bowl, toss the plum wedges with 1/3 cup granulated sugar, cornstarch, cardamom, lemon zest, vanilla, and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Let stand for 5 minutes, then toss again so no dry cornstarch remains.

instructions.name: Fill and fold the galette
instructions.text: Leaving excess liquid in the bowl, mound the plums in the center of the chilled pastry, keeping a 2-inch border. Arrange a few wedges cut-side up. Fold the border over the fruit in loose pleats, patching any cracks with your fingers. Return the pan to the freezer for 5 minutes if the dough has become soft.

instructions.name: Finish the crust
instructions.text: Beat the egg with 1 tablespoon water. Brush the exposed pastry lightly with egg wash, then sprinkle with the sliced almonds, coarse sugar, and remaining 1 tablespoon granulated sugar. Keep the egg wash off the parchment so the crust releases cleanly.

instructions.name: Bake and cool
instructions.text: Bake at 400°F for 40 to 45 minutes, rotating the pan after 25 minutes, until the crust is deeply golden and the plum juices bubble thickly for at least 2 minutes near the center. Cool on the pan for 20 minutes before slicing so the cornstarch can set the juices.

why_it_works: Cold yogurt hydrates the dough while its acidity and thickness limit gluten development, producing a tender crust without a long rest.
Leaving loose plum juice in the mixing bowl prevents the center from becoming sodden while the measured cornstarch thickens what the fruit releases in the oven.
Deep browning and visibly bubbling juices are more reliable doneness signals than a pale timer-only bake.
swaps: Replace up to half the plums with nectarines of similar ripeness and keep the total prepared fruit at 1 1/2 pounds.
For a nut-free galette, replace the almond flour with 1/4 cup all-purpose flour and omit the sliced almonds.
Use 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon instead of cardamom for a more familiar warm-spice profile.
storage: Keep the cooled galette loosely covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat slices on a sheet pan at 325°F for 8 to 10 minutes to re-crisp the crust. Freeze fully cooled slices in an airtight container for up to 2 months and reheat from frozen at 325°F for 15 to 18 minutes.
notes: Choose plums that yield slightly at the shoulder but are firm enough to slice; very soft plums release too much liquid.
A few cracks at the folded edge are fine. Pinch any opening that would let juice run directly onto the pan.
The calorie and cost estimates are per one-eighth galette and exclude optional ice cream or whipped cream.

faqs.q: Can I make the pastry ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Form it into a disk, wrap tightly, and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Let it stand for 5 to 10 minutes only if it is too firm to roll, then continue with the 15-minute freezer step.

A small amount of caramelized juice is normal. Heavy leaking usually means the fruit was overly ripe, loose juice was poured onto the dough, or a fold was left open. Use firm-ripe plums and patch obvious gaps before baking.

faqs.q: Can I bake this in a pie plate?
faqs.a: A rimmed sheet pan gives the bottom more direct heat and preserves the free-form shape. A metal pie plate works in a pinch, but the crust may need an extra 5 minutes to brown underneath.
